summary: ChatComposer: the agent chat's message box — an attachment tray above a bg-field frame holding an auto-growing textarea and a control row. Two arrangements, ONE DOM: inline is the sheet's radius-full pill, stacked squares to radius-xl the moment the text wraps, and the switch is flex-wrap + `order-first` rather than a different tree, so focus and the caret survive a wrap. `layout` defaults to `auto` and MEASURES the rendered line boxes — the sheet's rule is about the text wrapping, which only layout knows; the two literals exist for stories, baselines and callers who have already decided. Height is measured from scrollHeight and capped at `maxRows` (8) lines, then scrolls. Enter submits, Shift+Enter opens a line, and an Enter committing an IME candidate does neither — dispatched directly in the browser test, because userEvent cannot produce isComposing. The composer never clears itself: a send that failed has to be able to put the draft back. Add and Dictate are ELEMENT slots (Button ghost md full at the call site, because what Add opens is the caller's menu); Send/Stop is the component's, since it carries conversation state. isDropActive is presentational and documented as such — in a chat the drop target is the thread, so the composer draws the state and the app owns the event, which is also why this component starts no pointer gesture. THREE DESIGN DEFECTS FIXED IN PAPER. (1) The compact frame declared a 56px height on top of its p-md, a SECOND author of the inset: the vertical gap laid out at 12 against the 13.5 its padding declares, while the horizontal gap — which nothing else authored — was 13.5. Tabs' defect exactly, found by the new geometry spec. All 24 composer frames are now fit-content; the frame is 59 in Paper and 58 in Chromium, and the browser test asserts the four insets rather than the total. (2) The Stop control was drawn --ui-bg-emphasis, which IS the accent and which theme zero pins to neutral-0 in BOTH schemes — identical to the dark scheme's bg-field, so the control measured 1:1 there. The sheet raised it as a Conflict naming bg-inverse; that role is minted here rather than inverting emphasis, which Tooltip also depends on and whose own doc says an implementer must not pick it. (3) griddy's Stop glyph hard-codes a black fill (as Pause and every ChatCircle* do) and cannot take the ink; check:licensing rejects it. Shipped and redrawn as a filled SquareRounded. One deliberate override of a primitive: the empty Send keeps the sheet's bg-sunken fill instead of Button's disabled bg-elevated, which measures 1.03:1 on a white field and disappears — asserted against painted probes, and recorded in needsDesign so the two can be reconciled once.
